newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE firm to run Dubai waste oil plant - paper.
newsitem.headline: UAE firm to run Dubai waste oil plant - paper.

text.p: UAE firm Transtrade will operate a small waste oil refinery in Dubai for the next three months after its original operator went into receivership, the UAE Gulf News newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The private refinery was placed under receivership earlier this year when Western Oil Co, part of India's Gadgil Western Corp, defaulted on debt repayments to banks estimated at more than 10 million UAE dirhams ($2.7 million).
"The takeover by Transtrade conforms to efforts by the consortium of banks to liquidate Gadgil Western's outstandings in a phased manner," the paper reported.
The refinery, at Dubai's Jebel Ali free trade zone, was first operated as a fuel oil upgrading plant when it opened in 1995 with the aim of producing petroleum products.
It was converted last year into a waste oil recycling plant producing lubricants after failing to make a return.
Transtrade was examining the option of processing slop oil -- residue from oil tankers -- at the site, the paper said.
The paper quoted sources as saying that the refinery would run at a capacity of 65 tonnes a day.
Gadgil Western planned to process 125,000 tonnes a year at the plant.
